links.note: Greek adds or not to the question; English leaves the alternative implicit.
Greek asks whose son among you, recast with a repeated possessive in English.
Greek says honor will be yours, recast as you will be honored.
Greek says they invite you in return, rendered as returning the favor.
Greek says they do not have to repay, with resources left implicit.
Greek says eat bread, rendered here as feast.
English supplies everything for the implicit plural subject.
Must is supplied in the English.
Greek explicitly adds here after bring in; English leaves the destination implicit.
Greek uses hate; English renders it as disregard.
Greek says has for completion, with sufficient resources implicit.
Greek uses a passive seasoning verb, recast with an indefinite you.
